newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Low rates, good rains boost Zimbabwe shares.
newsitem.headline: Low rates, good rains boost Zimbabwe shares.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks traded largely firmer on Wednesday with brokers attributing continued positive investor sentiment to good rains and low interest rates on the local money market.
"The (stock) market is still very active and firm and this can be attributed to the current downward trend in inflation and interst rates," commented one broker.
"Also, the rains so far indicate a good agriculture season and if agriculture does well, the Zimbabwe economy does well," he added.

Counters to advance on Wednesday included bankers Barclays and window and door manufacturers Radar, both 10 cents up at 2,360 and 360 respectively, while building and engineering firm Mashonaland Holdings and CIH each put on 15 cents to 250 and 95 cents respectively.

Further gains in Tobacco Sales Limited, 20 cents firmer at 680, sugar grower Hippo, which gained 25 cents to 1,000 and plate and glass company PGI, which added 40 cents to 500, pushed the key 57-counter industrial index 33.84 points up to 8,517.40.

In minings, nickel producer Bindura traded unchanged at 800 but a five cent gain in gold miner Falgold and coal giant Wankie, which went up 30 cents to 500, nudged the seven share index 15.58 points up to 1,035.02.
